text:
tasha: Heads-up — hit intermittent INF / huge-logit spikes in production-like runs of the fused attention variant when KV cache is warm and bf16 is enabled on A100. Repro + short logs below.

kevin: ugh, ok. how often? single request or after long streaming?

tasha: very rare (~1/5k requests in our 2xprod-replay bench). Happens after many incremental writes to KV (long rollouts, seq_len ~ 4096). Root cause seems tied to kernel choice switching to the 'wide-tile' fused kernel.

maria: can you paste the minimal repro command?

tasha: sure — this is what I used on a single GPU dev box:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=./lib python -m bench.attn \\  --variant fused_widetile \\  --seq-len 4096 \\  --batch 2 \\  --dtype bf16 \\  --kv-cache \\  --warmup 200 \\  --iters 2000
```

perf-bot: profile ID 2026-03-02_1755 attached (nvtx + cupy traces).

tasha: small excerpt of the stdout from the failing run:

```
[t=120s] step 1376: max_logit=1.23e+04, softmax_max=1.23e+04, exp_clamp=inf
[t=120s] step 1376: output contains infs (first inf at out[0,11,2103])
Runtime: selected kernel=fused_widetile, tile=(64,128), fp_mode=bf16
```

kevin: interesting — large max_logit before softmax => exp overflow. Usually we expect softmax-stabilizer to subtract max per row; maybe the fused kernel missed the reduce across the right axis?

maria: two hypotheses: 1) numeric drift in bf16 accumulators vs fp16 path; 2) slice-alignment bug when merging KV pages causing garbage values.

tasha: i debugged that — after dumping the QKV tiles before the kernel, the values looked sane (< 20). The spike occurs inside the dot-product accumulation.

kevin: could be mantissa rollover during accumulation at large sequence lengths. bf16 has 7 mantissa bits effectively? that gives low dynamic range for a running sum of 4096 terms.

maria: right — and if the kernel uses an FP16 accumulator (or does a fused multiply accumulate with limited intermediate range) a rare pattern of signs could push it into a huge positive before the row-max subtraction.

tasha: i ran the same bench forcing the tiled kernel to use fp32 accumulation (env: ATTN_ACCUM_FP32=1) and the issue vanished after 20k iterations. No infs. Perf hit ~+12% latency but stable.

kevin: good repro. two immediate mitigation options:
- force fp32 accumulation for the wide-tile fused kernel (config flag)
- add a numeric guard in kernel selector: if seq_len*kv_scale > threshold -> prefer fp32-accum kernel

maria: also consider adding per-row partial reductions (i.e., compute max in chunks) so the max subtraction happens before large accumulations. That buys dynamic range without full fp32. Might be a good middle ground.

tasha: we should also add a runtime soft-fallback: detect when output contains NaN/inf and immediately re-run the request with safe kernel (fp32-accum or paged-flash). That avoids customer-visible errors.

perf-bot: microbenchmark numbers (quick):
- fused_widetile bf16 default: p50=12.4ms, p99=18.9ms
- fused_widetile bf16 w/ATTN_ACCUM_FP32=1: p50=13.9ms, p99=21.1ms
- paged_flash bf16 (safe): p50=15.6ms, p99=24.4ms

kevin: acceptable for now. plan: add selector guard + detection fallback. Also add unit test that runs a replay trace for 100k steps to trigger the condition in CI.

maria: i'll prototype chunked-max in the fused kernel and run a correctness sweep across bf16/fp16. If that fixes it we can keep bf16 perf and avoid full fp32.

tasha: opened an issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-8312 (repro + logs + profile link). Assigning to eng-runtime.

kevin: next steps for this thread:
- eng-runtime: add kernel-selector gating (kevin)
- eng-ml: run numeric sweep on blender workloads to check for quality regressions (maria)
- eng-oncall: add an alert for repeated infs in outputs (tasha)

tasha: thanks. i'll push the failing-case test into the perf repo under canaries so we don't regress silently.

maria: quick note — if we add fallback re-run, cap it to 1 retry to avoid doubling cost; also add rate limit per key.

kevin: agreed. i'll PR patch for selector + detection today. tagging @everyone in eng-runtime: please review the numeric guard change when it's up. :eyes:

tasha: thanks all — i'll paste links to bench runs / flamegraphs once uploads finish. :thumbsup:
